generator_reasoning: It lists exactly whom the appointee must notify on discovering a conflict with one of the affected attorney's clients, and directs him to the professional conduct rules.

query: Closed civil file is stuffed with discovery materials nobody needs. Does clearing them out take a stipulation or a motion, or can the clerk get that started on her own?

query: Child protective trial coming up and we want the courtroom cleared and the girl kept from having to look at her father while she testifies. Is that something I have to flag in writing beforehand?
generator_reasoning: It is the item on the advance-notice list covering a request to close the courtroom or block the respondent from the witness's view.

query: The panel's published opinion can't be squared with an earlier one out of a different panel. What do I lean on as my ground for taking it up to the high court?
generator_reasoning: It is the ground for leave that rests on the decision being irreconcilable with a Supreme Court or another Court of Appeals decision.

query: Girl removed at the preliminary hearing had been living with her grandmother under a guardianship, not with either parent. Does the judge have to take up grandma's contact with her right then?
generator_reasoning: It requires the court at that hearing to decide what contact, if any, the guardian or legal custodian the child had been living with will get.

query: Estate is already open and my client, a beneficiary, wants to raise something new. Can she just file her own petition and get it on the docket, and who has to be served?
generator_reasoning: It lets an interested person file a petition on a new matter and get a hearing, and specifies service on the fiduciary and other interested persons.

query: The e-filing portal has been down since yesterday with no restoration date. Where would that be announced, and am I still on the hook for tomorrow's deadline?
generator_reasoning: It requires notice on the designated statewide websites during an extended outage and puts the burden back on filers to file and serve on paper to meet deadlines.

query: Defense is fighting the restitution figure that came in with the presentence report. Who carries the burden on what the victim actually lost, and to what level of proof?
generator_reasoning: It assigns the prosecutor the burden of showing the victim's loss and fixes the standard the judge uses to settle a restitution fight.

query: Do the earlier versions of my expert's answers to the standard expert interrogatories have to be handed over, or are they shielded the way trial-prep material is?
generator_reasoning: It extends work-product protection to earlier versions of the expert interrogatory answers no matter how they were recorded.

validation.note: The question is answerable by this provision, but MCR 2.302(B)(3)(a) is a co-valid answer because it defines the trial-prep shield that the user explicitly asks about, so it should be added to the gold labels.

query: Does the body that investigates complaints against judges have to have a written policy on what it keeps, how long it keeps it, and how it gets rid of it?
generator_reasoning: It requires that commission to adopt a retention policy covering stored materials, retention periods, and disposal procedures.

query: There is a procedure sitting in an old statute that the court rules simply do not address. Is it still good law, or did the adoption of the rules wipe it out?
generator_reasoning: It keeps statutory practice provisions in force so long as they do not conflict with the rules, until the Supreme Court supersedes them.

query: Child was already adjudicated and living at home; we picked him up on an emergency and the 24-hour hearing is this afternoon. What does the judge have to reduce to writing, and does mom get to speak to it?
generator_reasoning: It requires a written finding that the placement criteria are met and gives the parent the chance to say why the child should not be taken or should go back.

query: We want to take the other side's offer of judgment. How long is the window, and what exactly do I have to get to the court to have judgment entered on it?
generator_reasoning: It sets the 21-day window from service and lists the notice of agreement, the offer, and proof of service as what must be served and filed for judgment to enter.

query: Sheriff seized my client's equipment under a writ of attachment. Who puts a value on the seized items, and how many people have to sign off on that valuation?
generator_reasoning: It requires the officer to inventory the seized property and two disinterested county residents, sworn beforehand, to appraise and sign.

query: District court misdemeanor trial, we seated eight. When do we cut it down to the six who actually decide, and if I have to sub an alternate in mid-deliberation what do I tell the jury?
generator_reasoning: It authorizes the extra jurors, fixes the point at which names are drawn to bring the panel down to six, and requires deliberations to restart when an alternate steps in.

query: The department just notified us it is cutting off extended guardianship assistance for the young man in our juvenile guardianship. Does ending the guardianship take a motion and a hearing, or does the court act on that notice alone?
generator_reasoning: It directs the court to end the juvenile guardianship at once on receiving that notice, without the motion-and-hearing route.

query: Clerk quoted a per-page copy charge that looks like it bakes in what the county spent on its imaging system. Are they allowed to pass that along?
generator_reasoning: It limits the charge to actual labor, supplies, and system use and expressly excludes the cost of buying and maintaining the technology.

query: Circuit court file was destroyed in a flood. Once the judge accepts our reconstructed copies, are those treated as the real thing going forward or just a working substitute?
generator_reasoning: This subrule directs entry of the order accepting the substitute and says the substitute carries the same force as the original while the original remains lost.

query: Client wants firearms taken from her ex. Can I bring that request by motion in the divorce file that's already open, or does it have to be its own case, and is there a fee?
generator_reasoning: The provision states that this kind of action is a stand-alone filing in the family division, cannot be raised by motion in an existing case, and carries no filing fee.

query: Judge says he's putting this trust under court supervision. Does he have to spell out what that actually entails, or is the order just a label?
generator_reasoning: It requires the court, when it orders supervision during a trust proceeding, to state the terms of that supervision.

query: Drafting a delinquency petition for a kid who lives with his aunt under a guardianship. Do I name her in the petition or only the parents?
generator_reasoning: It requires the petition to name and give the address of the guardian, legal custodian, or person having custody when that is someone other than a parent.

query: One of the sitting members of the body that disciplines judges is himself the subject of the complaint before it. Is he automatically off that matter, and what else knocks a member off?
generator_reasoning: It disqualifies a member judge or justice from acting in that capacity in a matter about his own conduct and imports the general judicial disqualification grounds.

validation.note: The question is fully answerable from the provided text, but because it explicitly asks 'what else knocks a member off', MCR 2.003(C) is a co-valid answer that a retriever would need to find to completely resolve the query.

query: Designation hearing is being set while everyone is standing in the courtroom. Can the judge just announce the date on the record, or does something have to go out in the mail?
generator_reasoning: It permits notice of the designation hearing to be given orally on the record, by mail, or by any other means reasonably calculated to reach those entitled to it.

query: Commitment order for an infectious disease case expires next month and the hospital wants it extended. Who files, how far ahead, and how long can the new order run?
generator_reasoning: This subrule sets the 14-day advance filing, names the facility director as the moving party, and caps any commitment order at six months.

query: Personal representative wants to sue somebody. In probate court, when a matter has to be brought that way rather than by petition, how is it started and what does the caption say?
generator_reasoning: This subrule identifies the matters that must be captioned as civil actions, begun by complaint, and run under circuit court civil practice.

query: Circuit court just granted the other side leave to appeal a district court judgment. I want to cross appeal. How long do I have?
generator_reasoning: This provision fixes the cross appeal window for an appellee at 14 days from service of the order granting leave in circuit court appeals.

query: The divorce judgment and the separate support form we submitted say different things about the monthly amount. Which one controls, and did both need the judge's signature?
generator_reasoning: This subrule requires the standardized support order to accompany and be signed alongside the judgment and makes it controlling over conflicting judgment terms.

query: Settled a minor's injury claim for $40,000 lump sum. What has to be in place in probate before the circuit judge will sign the dismissal, and who does the check get made out to?
generator_reasoning: This provision sets the dollar threshold requiring a conservator, directs payment to the conservator, and conditions entry of the judgment on written verification of the bond.

query: Opposing side is self-represented but a lawyer just filed a limited appearance for her. Do I keep copying the party on everything, or is serving the lawyer enough now?
generator_reasoning: This provision requires continued service on the party plus service on the limited scope attorney, with a court option to relieve the party from service.

query: Our friend of the court keeps getting mail returned for one parent. Can the office update the address in the file on its own without anyone filing a motion, and under what authority?
generator_reasoning: This subrule authorizes the friend of the court to change a party's address administratively under a policy set by the state court administrator.

query: Presentence report came back with no mention of my client's juvenile record. Is that something it's supposed to cover, or is it adult convictions only?
generator_reasoning: This item requires the presentence report to describe both prior adult convictions and juvenile adjudications.

query: Misdemeanor sentencing in district court. Does the judge have to invite my client himself to say something before pronouncing sentence, or is defense counsel speaking enough?
generator_reasoning: This subprovision is the district court sentencing requirement that the judge speak to the defendant directly and let the defendant offer mitigation.

validation.note: The question is fully answerable by this provision, but MCR 6.425(D)(2) is the more generally applicable sentencing rule that also directly answers this question.

query: Post-sentence motion, and the judge agrees the plea colloquy was defective. Does that vacate the plea automatically or does my client get to choose?
generator_reasoning: This subrule requires the court to cure the defect on the record and then let the defendant elect between keeping the plea and sentence or withdrawing.

query: Contested guardianship in probate. Are we on the hook for the automatic exchange of information that starts a circuit court civil case, and can I serve discovery on an interested person who isn't formally a party?
generator_reasoning: This subrule applies the civil discovery subchapter in probate while carving out mandatory initial disclosures and treating interested persons as parties.

query: Prosecutor wants a designated case on a home invasion, first degree. Is that automatically one of the qualifying offenses or does something more have to be true?
generator_reasoning: This item conditions first-degree home invasion's inclusion in the qualifying-offense list on the juvenile being armed with a dangerous weapon as statutorily defined.

query: Delinquency preliminary hearing. Can the court weigh the fact that this kid has hurt people before when deciding whether to hold him?
generator_reasoning: This listed factor is the juvenile's past conduct resulting in physical harm to others, which the court must consider in the detention decision.

query: Can we send a filing to the court by fax in a child protective proceeding, and if so which rule sets out the mechanics?
generator_reasoning: This rule permits fax filing of records in juvenile matters and routes the procedure to the general facsimile filing rule.

query: Defendant is a minor and nobody has put forward anyone to stand in for her. How long after service do we wait before moving to have the court name someone?
generator_reasoning: This item permits appointment on motion of the court or a party once 21 days have run from service with no nomination made or approved.

query: Who names the chair of the body that prosecutes attorney misconduct, how long is the term, and can the same person be kept on?
generator_reasoning: This subrule gives the Supreme Court the designation power over the grievance commission's chair and vice-chair, sets one-year terms, and addresses reappointment and midterm vacancies.

query: Ancient case that has been pending since before the current rules came in. Is there any way for the judge to let it keep running under the old procedure?
generator_reasoning: This rule sets the effective date, applies the rules to pending matters, and lets a court allow a pending action to continue under the former rules where applying them is unworkable or unjust.

query: Employer already has a higher-priority income withholding running on this debtor when our periodic writ lands. Do they withhold nothing for us until that one ends?
generator_reasoning: This provision says the lower priority writ yields, except that with earnings the garnishee must still withhold up to the legal maximum not consumed by the higher priority order.

query: Respondent attorney is raising addiction in mitigation and asking for probation. Can the panel force him to be evaluated, and what happens if he won't sit for it?
generator_reasoning: This subrule lets the panel order an examination, allocate its cost to the respondent, and disqualifies a refusing respondent from probation.

query: Apart from the degree and practice-experience piece, is there a course someone has to finish before serving as a mediator in a divorce case, and who signs off on it?
generator_reasoning: This item requires completion of a training program approved by the State Court Administrator covering domestic relations mediation skills.

query: Does the body that handles judicial misconduct do anything besides investigate complaints, like putting out ethics training for judges?
generator_reasoning: This rule directs the commission to develop educational materials and programs with other organizations to support judges' understanding of their ethical duties.

query: Final pretrial is set. Can I send the associate who has been covering motions, or does it have to be the lawyer who will actually try it?
generator_reasoning: This subrule requires at least one lead trial attorney for each party, plus any unrepresented party, to attend the final pretrial conference.

query: We are holding a commitment hearing on the hospital unit instead of at the courthouse. Is there anything required about the setting itself?
generator_reasoning: This subrule obligates the court to secure a quiet, dignified, undisturbed setting when the hearing is held outside its usual courtroom.

query: Partition property went at auction in three separate lots to different bidders. What does the post-sale report to the court have to say about the split?
generator_reasoning: This item requires the report of sale to describe which parcels went to each purchaser.

query: Discovery materials we actually lodged with the clerk -- do those count as part of the court's record, or are they treated as something outside it?
generator_reasoning: This subrule lists what is included as court records, expressly covering discovery materials and other materials filed with the clerk.

query: Won a motion to compel. Is the court stuck with ordering the answers and costs, or can it go further and hit their claims?
generator_reasoning: This subrule authorizes additional just sanctions on a motion to compel, including the merits-affecting orders listed elsewhere in the rule.

validation.note: While the question is answerable and realistic, MCR 2.313(B)(2) provides the specific list of sanctions (including striking claims) that the court can order, making it a better target citation than the general catch-all provision in subrule (A)(6).

query: Plaintiff's initial disclosures -- does the clock run from when I filed the complaint, or from when the defendant answers?
generator_reasoning: This subrule ties the pleading party's disclosure deadline to 14 days after an opposing party files an answer to that pleading.

query: Everyone signed off on the case evaluation number. If my client just writes the check right away, does a judgment still get entered against it?
generator_reasoning: This subrule provides that payment of the award within 28 days of notification of the acceptances results in dismissal with prejudice rather than entry of judgment.

query: Clerk refused to accept our filing. What are the only grounds a clerk is allowed to reject a document on?
generator_reasoning: This subrule enumerates the exclusive bases for rejection at the counter and exempts court-generated documents from rejection.

query: Trustee is presenting an account on a living trust that the settlor can still revoke. Who has to be given notice -- the settlor, or the people who would take when he dies?
generator_reasoning: This subrule identifies who counts as interested in an accounting proceeding when the trust is revocable, which differs from the irrevocable-trust list.

query: Probate matter and I can't find one of the heirs. What has to go in front of the court before I can notice him in the newspaper, and do I have to keep republishing at every later stage?
generator_reasoning: This subrule conditions publication on a verified declaration showing diligent inquiry and limits later notice to persons whose addresses are known.

query: First-party no-fault case. Without waiting for any request, what does the plaintiff have to turn over about what's still owed to the treaters?
generator_reasoning: This subrule is the disclosure item requiring the plaintiff to produce provider bills and outstanding balances for which reimbursement is sought.

query: Our circuit is writing its ADR plan and wants to route cases out to the community mediation center. What does the court have to weigh before setting that up, and can the plan override parties who want to pick their own mediator?
generator_reasoning: This subrule authorizes referral relationships with dispute resolution centers, lists the factors courts must consider, and preserves the parties' right to select their own mediator.

query: Resident with a developmental disability was brought back to the center after a leave that ran more than ten days. Who has to tell the court, how quickly, and who else has to be told they can challenge the return?
generator_reasoning: This subrule sets the center director's 24-hour notification duties and the court's obligation to notify the guardian and, for a minor, the parents.

query: Governor has asked the Supreme Court to take up a controlling public-law question that is sitting in a trial court right now. How does that question get up there, and what happens to the case below in the meantime?
generator_reasoning: This subrule describes certification of the question on executive message of the governor and the stay of further proceedings below.

query: PPO respondent is a road deputy who has to carry a firearm for his job and wants the order changed. Is he still stuck giving the petitioner a full week's notice before the hearing?
generator_reasoning: This subrule sets the ordinary seven-day service requirement and makes one day's notice sufficient where the moving respondent must carry a weapon for employment.

query: Attorney was moved to inactive status over a disability years ago and wants back in. How often can he ask, what does he have to prove, and is there anything extra after being out that long?
generator_reasoning: This subrule governs restoration to active status: annual petitions, proof by clear and convincing evidence that the disability is gone, and recertification after three years inactive.

query: Who actually decides what hours our court runs and how many judges and staff have to be on hand at any given time?
generator_reasoning: This subrule assigns the chief judge the authority to set court and judge hours and to determine and require staffing levels.

query: Defendant never showed and we're taking a default judgment. Is there something about his service status I have to put in the file before the judge signs?
generator_reasoning: This subrule requires the nonmilitary affidavit to be filed before judgment is entered against a defendant who has not appeared.

query: Client pleaded no contest. At sentencing, what does the judge have to tell him about getting to the Court of Appeals -- is it an appeal he can just take?

query: Case settled while it's pending in the Supreme Court. Can the parties just stipulate it away, and is there any exposure if we do it right before the argument session?
generator_reasoning: This rule allows a stipulated administrative dismissal, lets the Court refuse it in a matter set for argument, and permits costs when the stipulation arrives within 21 days of the session.

query: Deposition is done and no one has asked for a transcript. Does the reporter have to produce one anyway?
generator_reasoning: This subrule provides that the testimony need not be transcribed unless a party requests it.

query: Defense wants to point the finger at somebody who isn't in the case. How long after our answer do we have to say so, and is there any relief if the facts only surfaced later?
generator_reasoning: This subrule fixes the 91-day filing period measured from the party's first responsive pleading and states the standard for permitting a late notice.

query: Client had her fees waived in her custody file and now she's got a separate landlord-tenant case. Does that waiver carry over, or does she start again?

query: Court-ordered mediation and the parties never worked out who pays. How does the mediator's bill get split?
generator_reasoning: This subrule provides that mediation costs are divided pro rata absent agreement or a court order otherwise.

query: If we get a money judgment reversed and reinstated on appeal, what rate of interest runs on it for the period the case was on appeal?
generator_reasoning: Judgment interest rates are fixed by statute (MCL 600.6013), not by any Michigan Court Rule.

query: Supreme Court turned down our application. How long do I have to ask them to look again, and if that gets denied can I take another run at it?
generator_reasoning: This subrule sets the 21-day period from certification of the order and bars a successive motion directed at an order denying reconsideration.

query: Civil jury trial. Can the defense hold its opening until it starts putting on proofs, and can we skip openings altogether if everyone is on board?
generator_reasoning: This subrule lets the adverse party give its statement either right after the opening party's or immediately before its own evidence, and allows waiver with the court's and opposing counsel's consent.

query: Caseworker wants legal advice partway through an abuse and neglect case. Is the prosecutor required to advise the department if asked?
generator_reasoning: This subrule obligates the prosecuting attorney, on request, to act as legal consultant to the department or its contracted agent throughout a child protective proceeding.

query: Bond was set down in district court. Once we're arraigned on the information, does the circuit judge have to defer to that, or can she take a completely fresh look without me showing anything has changed?
generator_reasoning: This subrule authorizes a de novo determination and modification of a prior release decision at and after the arraignment on the information.

query: Juvenile arraigned on a complaint and warrant. How soon does the preliminary examination have to be set, and does an adjournment the prosecutor already used in the family division cut into that time?
generator_reasoning: This subrule sets the 14-day window for the preliminary examination and credits up to three days of a special adjournment already taken under the juvenile rule.

query: All counsel have approved the form of the order. Does that mean the judge has to sign it?
generator_reasoning: This subrule directs the court to sign an order whose form all parties have approved, provided it matches what the court decided.

query: Adult guardianship hearing coming up — can the judge rely on the examining clinician's written evaluation without putting that person on the stand, and how far ahead of the hearing does it have to be on file?
generator_reasoning: This subrule sets both the conditions for receiving the examiner's written report in place of testimony and the filing lead time.

query: Drafting a divorce complaint. How much detail do I plead about why the marriage broke down -- do I lay out the specific facts?
generator_reasoning: This subrule requires the grounds to be pleaded, but in divorce and separate maintenance to be stated in the statutory language without further particulars.

query: Juvenile being prosecuted in circuit court as an adult and the court wants the father to pay for the appointed defense lawyer. What has to happen before that order can be enforced against him?
generator_reasoning: This subrule authorizes assessing representation costs against a person responsible for the juvenile's support and conditions enforceability on a hearing opportunity plus service of the order.

query: Who does the Supreme Court have to give advance word to before it changes a court rule, and where would the public see the proposal and the comment deadline?
generator_reasoning: This subrule identifies who must be notified of a proposed amendment, that the comment manner and date accompany the notice, and that it is posted on the Court's website.

query: I want to run my own recorder during a hearing so I can use it while I'm trying the case. Do I need the judge's permission, and can I do anything with the audio afterward?
generator_reasoning: This subrule governs recordings made by an attorney or self-represented party — permission on motion, court control of the manner, and use limited to the proceeding recorded and never publicly.

query: Small claims trial and both sides are present. Can a party take part remotely by video, and what does the court need to push the trial to a later date?
generator_reasoning: This subrule both authorizes videoconferencing for small claims participants and supplies the good-cause standard for adjourning the trial.

query: When a solo practitioner dies or is suddenly unable to practice and someone has to stand in for him, can a whole firm be designated, or does it have to be one individual lawyer?
generator_reasoning: This definition covers both an individual active Michigan attorney in good standing and a law firm with at least one other active attorney.

query: Lawyer placed on probation because of an impairment — what's the ceiling on how long that can run, can it be stretched further, and how many shots does he get at ending it early?
generator_reasoning: This subrule sets the 3-year cap, the extension limit, the conditions for dissolution, and the one-motion limit on accelerating dissolution.

query: On the quarterly criminal caseload report the chief judge sends the state court administrator, how long does a misdemeanor or ordinance case have to sit before it has to be listed, and from what event is that counted?
generator_reasoning: This subrule sets the delay threshold for misdemeanor and criminal ordinance cases and identifies the start point as the defendant's first appearance on the warrant and complaint or citation.

query: Opposing side's appeal is nothing but a stall. What do I have to convince the Court of Appeals of to get damages assessed for it?
generator_reasoning: This subrule states the ground — an appeal brought to hinder or delay, or with no reasonable basis for believing there is a meritorious issue.

query: Once a video deposition is actually filed with the court, who holds the recording, and what has to happen for it to sit somewhere other than the courthouse?
generator_reasoning: This subrule governs custody after filing, the limited grounds for storage elsewhere, the sealing requirement in the storage order, and the status of filed video depositions.

query: Prelim on a juvenile charged under the automatic waiver statute — the magistrate finds no probable cause on the qualifying charge but does find it on a lesser offense. Where does the case go, and do we have to pay for the exam transcript?
generator_reasoning: This subrule directs transfer to the family division in the county where the offense allegedly occurred and provides the preliminary examination transcript free on request.

query: Client wants to plead guilty but mentally ill. What does the judge have to do on top of the usual plea colloquy before that plea can be taken?
generator_reasoning: This rule adds to the ordinary plea requirements: examination of the psychiatric reports, a hearing supporting a mental illness finding at the time of the offense, and making the reports part of the record.

query: Protective proceeding — the man we noticed as the possible father denies it and names a different man as the real father. What can the court find as to that second man, and then what?
generator_reasoning: This subrule lets the court find probable cause that another identifiable person is the natural father and requires the same putative-father procedure to be run as to him.

query: Fee dispute with a former client and we're both willing to let the grievance administrator arbitrate it. What has to be in place first, and where does the award get filed?
generator_reasoning: This subrule requires a written agreement between attorney and client, applies the general arbitration rule, and directs where the award and motion for entry are filed.

query: E-filing is mandatory in this court and a self-represented party wants to keep filing on paper. He owns a computer but can barely manage email. Is that something the judge weighs?
generator_reasoning: This factor is one of the good-cause considerations and asks specifically about the person's technical ability to use and understand email and the filing software.

query: Just got appointed guardian ad litem in a juvenile case. Do I have to file something to get on the record, and does it have to disclose my connections to the child or the family?
generator_reasoning: This subrule requires a written appearance in the form the court designates and requires it to state any interest the guardian ad litem holds relating to the minor, the family, or others in the proceeding.

query: Outside group wants to weigh in supporting our application for leave in the Supreme Court. Do they need permission first, and how long do they have once the answer comes in?
generator_reasoning: This subrule requires a granted motion (subject to a narrow exception), sets the 21-day window keyed to the answer, and requires conformity with the amicus brief rule.

query: Disqualification motion was granted against a circuit judge who doesn't handle business court matters. Who gets the case next, and what happens if nobody else on that bench can take it?
generator_reasoning: This subrule covers reassignment within the same court for non-business-court judges outside the Supreme Court and provides for state court administrator assignment when no local judge is available.

query: Partition sale order already covers which parcels go, whether they sell together, and any floor price. What else does the judge have to fix if the buyer won't be paying all cash?
generator_reasoning: This item requires the order of sale to designate the terms of credit allowed and the security required.

query: Collaborative divorce is finished and we're filing the joint petition asking for entry of the judgment. Does a summons have to issue, and do the parties still file separate answers and appearances?
generator_reasoning: This subrule dispenses with the summons requirement and makes the petition serve as complaint, answer, and appearance of both attorneys.

query: Case evaluation panel found the defendant's defense frivolous and he never put up the required bond. What happens to that defendant, and does the rest of the case still get tried?
generator_reasoning: This subrule directs entry of default against a defendant whose defense was frivolous when no bond is posted, and provides that trial proceeds on remaining claims and on damages against the defaulted defendant.
